specs.title: CSV export
sources: Spec 'CSV export' version 2, approved (dl-015)
QA report: the spec is silent on exports of more than 100,000 rows; the current code times out
Current code behaviour: an export above 100,000 rows times out
in_scope: The behaviour when an export would contain more than 100,000 rows
non_goals: Any change to the criteria of version 2 other than the added large-export criterion

criteria.text: Criteria 1 to N of version 2 stand unchanged and keep their numbers and checks.
criteria.check: As stated in version 2

criteria.text: (New, numbered after the last version-2 criterion) Given a filter that matches more than 100,000 rows, when the user requests the export, then the result is the behaviour the owner chooses in open question 1; in no option does the request end in an unexplained timeout.
criteria.check: Integration test with a fixture of 100,001 rows asserting the chosen behaviour; boundary test with exactly 100,000 rows asserting the normal export

open_questions.question: What should the user get when an export would contain more than 100,000 rows?

options.option: Refuse with a message asking to narrow the filter
options.changes: Smallest change; large reconciliations need several exports

options.option: Produce the file in the background and deliver a download link when ready
options.changes: Full data in one file; adds a background job and a notification path, larger line

options.option: Split into several files of at most 100,000 rows each
options.changes: Full data, synchronous limits remain; users must combine files

options.option: Raise the limit so such exports complete synchronously
options.changes: Needs a stated new limit and performance work; the problem recurs above the new limit

versions: 3 (2026-11-27): adds the behaviour above 100,000 rows after the QA report; version 2 is not edited; work built against version 2 is to be checked against version 3

actions_now: Ask the owner in chat which large-export behaviour they want, with the options and their consequences, and open version 3 as a draft carrying the question; version 2 stays as approved. Once the owner answers, fill criterion 2 from their words, record the decision, and submit version 3 for the owner's approval; QA's other checks against version 2 can continue.

specs.title: CSV export
sources: Spec 'CSV export' version 1, approved (dl-014)
Implementer report: the reports API returns no emails and adding them is outside this line
Current behaviour of the reports API: no customer email field
in_scope: Everything in version 1 except criterion 3, which waits on the open question
non_goals: Changing the reports API inside this line

criteria.text: Criteria of version 1 other than 3 stand unchanged and keep their numbers and checks.
criteria.check: As stated in version 1

criteria.text: Given an export, when it is generated, then the customer's email is included or excluded as the owner decides in open question 1.
criteria.check: Integration test asserting the presence or absence of the email column per the decision

expected_areas: Possibly the reports API, only if the owner chooses to extend it (as a separate line)

open_questions.question: Criterion 3 requires the customer's email, which the reports API does not provide: how should the export treat it?

options.option: Drop the email from this export (version 2 without criterion 3)
options.changes: This line ships now without emails; anyone relying on the email in the export does not get it

options.option: Keep the email and add a separate line that extends the reports API to return it
options.changes: Criterion 3 waits for that line; adds personal data to an API and the export, which needs a privacy decision

options.option: Ship this line without the email now and add it later in a new version
options.changes: Partial delivery now; a later version and line for emails

open_questions.waiting_for: Owner (also a privacy decision, since emails are personal data)

versions: 2 (2026-11-27): criterion 3 made dependent on an owner question after the implementer's report; version 1 is not edited

actions_now: Send the owner the question on criterion 3 with its options and consequences, flagging that adding emails is a privacy matter, and open version 2 as a draft; tell the implementer that criteria other than 3 may proceed and criterion 3 waits. I do not drop or keep the email myself.

specs.title: Settings that follow the user across devices
sources: Owner request: users keep their theme and language settings across devices (the table named in the request is passed to the architect as a hint, not a requirement)
in_scope: The user's theme setting is kept for the user and applied on every device they sign in on
The user's language setting is kept for the user and applied on every device they sign in on
non_goals: Other settings beyond theme and language
How and where the settings are stored (architect's decision)

criteria.text: Given a signed-in user who sets the theme on device A, when they sign in on device B, then device B shows the theme they set.
criteria.check: End-to-end test with two sessions of the same user

criteria.text: Given a signed-in user who sets the language on device A, when they sign in on device B, then device B shows the interface in that language.
criteria.check: End-to-end test with two sessions of the same user

criteria.text: Given a user who has never set theme or language, when they sign in, then they see the default chosen in open question 1.
criteria.check: Integration test with a new user

criteria.text: Given a request to save a theme or language value that is not one the app offers, when it is submitted, then it is refused with an error and the stored setting is unchanged.
criteria.check: Negative API test

criteria.text: Given a user who changed a setting on two devices, when both are open, then the setting shown follows the rule chosen in open question 2.
criteria.check: End-to-end test with two concurrent sessions

criteria.text: Given a user who is not signed in, when they change theme or language, then the behaviour follows open question 3.
criteria.check: End-to-end test without a session

expected_areas: User account service and its storage
Session start-up where settings are applied

open_questions.question: What is the default theme and language for a user with no saved setting?

options.option: The app's current defaults
options.changes: No visible change for new users

options.option: Taken from the device or browser
options.changes: New users see their system theme and language; needs detection

open_questions.question: When the setting is changed on two devices, which wins and when does the other device update?

options.option: Last change wins, applied at next sign-in or reload
options.changes: Simplest; a device may show an old setting until reload

options.option: Last change wins, applied live to open sessions
options.changes: Consistent everywhere; needs a push or polling path

open_questions.question: What happens to settings changed while signed out?

options.option: Kept on that device only and not synced
options.changes: Signed-out behaviour stays as today

options.option: Carried into the account at next sign-in
options.changes: Device setting may overwrite the account setting; needs a merge rule

actions_now: Write the spec in terms of behaviour (settings follow the user across devices), passing the requested table to the architect only as a hint, and send the owner the three open questions. Criteria 1, 2 and 4 can be built once the spec is approved; 3, 5 and 6 wait on the answers.

Decline to write a spec: this is a bug fix with a known cause, and the expected behaviour is already defined by the page for users with an avatar, minus the image. I tell the factory the line goes straight to the implementer, with a regression test for a user without an avatar as its check.

Hand the complete draft to the coordinating session for provisional approval, since the binding gives it that leave and the product role cannot approve its own spec. Once the coordinating session approves, the spec is marked approved-provisional, with the approval cited as provisional in the decision queue waiting for the owner. Work starts with its units marked provisional: true, and every report states that the approval is provisional, not the owner's.

specs.title: Discount at checkout
sources: Owner request: 'Add a discount to checkout.'
in_scope: A discount applied to an order at checkout, with its size, eligibility and combination rules as the owner decides

criteria.text: Given an order that qualifies under the rule chosen in open question 2, when the customer reaches checkout, then the total is reduced by the amount chosen in open question 1 and the reduction is visible to the customer before payment.
criteria.check: Integration test of checkout totals for a qualifying order

criteria.text: Given an order that does not qualify, when the customer reaches checkout, then no discount is applied.
criteria.check: Negative integration test

criteria.text: Given an order that already carries another offer, when the customer reaches checkout, then the discount combines or not per open question 3.
criteria.check: Integration test with another offer applied

open_questions.question: How large is the discount?

options.option: A percentage of the order
options.changes: Scales with order value; needs a percentage and rounding rule

options.option: A fixed amount
options.changes: Same reduction for all; needs the amount, currency and a minimum order

open_questions.waiting_for: Owner (price decision; no provisional choice allowed)

open_questions.question: Who gets the discount?

options.option: Every customer
options.changes: Simple; affects all revenue

options.option: A group (e.g. first order, code holders, members)
options.changes: Needs an eligibility rule and possibly a code entry

open_questions.question: Does it combine with other offers?

options.option: Combines
options.changes: Larger total reductions possible; needs an order of application

options.option: Does not combine; the larger one applies
options.changes: Caps cost; needs a comparison rule

options.option: Does not combine; the existing offer applies
options.changes: Discount reaches fewer orders

actions_now: Write the draft with every criterion tied to an open question, and escalate to the owner, since this concerns money and the binding forbids provisional price choices. All criteria wait for the owner's answers; I pick no amount, audience or combination rule.

specs.title: Complete report exports for finance reconciliation
sources: Owner request: exports contain every column of the report so finance can reconcile
dl-009: personal emails never leave the system in any export
Current report: includes a Customer email column
in_scope: Exports include every column of the report, subject to how the conflict with dl-009 is resolved for Customer email

criteria.text: Given a report, when it is exported, then the export contains every column of the report other than Customer email, with the same values as the report.
criteria.check: Integration test comparing the export's columns and values with the report

criteria.text: Given a report with a Customer email column, when it is exported, then that column is treated as the owner decides in open question 1.
criteria.check: Integration test asserting the chosen treatment; if emails stay out, a negative test that no email address appears anywhere in the export

open_questions.question: The request (every column) contradicts dl-009 (no personal emails in any export) for the Customer email column: which prevails?

options.option: dl-009 prevails: Customer email is left out
options.changes: Complies with the recorded decision; finance reconciles without emails, which may or may not be enough

options.option: Replace the email with a non-personal identifier (e.g. customer id)
options.changes: Finance can match records without the email leaving; needs a decision that this satisfies dl-009

options.option: The owner revises dl-009 by a new recorded decision
options.changes: Emails included; a privacy decision recorded in the decision log, possibly with limits on who may export

actions_now: Write the draft and escalate the contradiction between the request and dl-009 to the owner as a privacy decision with the options side by side. Criterion 1 covers the non-email columns and can proceed once approved; criterion 2 waits for the answer.

specs.title: Colleagues' last-online time
sources: Team lead's request, passed on by the owner without comment: show each user when their colleagues were last online
in_scope: Showing a user the last-online time of their colleagues, within the visibility, opt-out and retention rules the owner decides
non_goals: Live online/offline status or activity tracking beyond the last-online time

criteria.text: Given a user permitted to see a colleague's last-online time under open question 1, when they view that colleague, then they see when the colleague was last online.
criteria.check: Integration test with a permitted viewer

criteria.text: Given a user not permitted under open question 1, when they view that colleague, then no last-online time is shown.
criteria.check: Negative authorization test, including a user from another organization

criteria.text: Given a colleague who has hidden their last-online time (if open question 2 allows it), when anyone views them, then no last-online time is shown.
criteria.check: Negative test with the hide setting on

criteria.text: Given last-online records older than the period chosen in open question 3, when the period passes, then they are no longer stored or shown.
criteria.check: Test with a mocked clock checking storage and display

open_questions.question: Who may see a user's last-online time?

options.option: Everyone in the same organization
options.changes: Widest exposure

options.option: Only the same team
options.changes: Needs team membership as the boundary

options.option: Only managers
options.changes: Turns it into monitoring; higher privacy and people risk

open_questions.question: Can users hide their last-online time?

options.option: Yes, opt-out
options.changes: Adds a setting; criterion 3 applies

options.option: Yes, off by default (opt-in)
options.changes: Fewer visible times; consent-first

options.option: No
options.changes: Criterion 3 drops; stronger privacy case needed

open_questions.question: How long is the last-online time kept?

options.option: Only the latest value, overwritten
options.changes: Minimal data kept

options.option: A history for a stated period
options.changes: More personal data; needs a retention period and deletion

actions_now: Write the draft and escalate to the owner, since visibility, opt-out and retention are decisions about privacy and people that the request leaves open. I also ask whether the owner adopts the team lead's request as their own. No criterion is built until those answers arrive.

specs.title: Dark mode
sources: Owner request: dark mode as a toggle on the settings page that applies to the whole app
in_scope: A dark-mode toggle on the settings page
Dark theme applied to every screen of the app when the toggle is on
non_goals: Themes other than light and dark

criteria.text: Given the settings page, when the user turns the toggle on, then every app screen renders in the dark theme without a reload of other screens being required to take effect on next navigation.
criteria.check: End-to-end test visiting each top-level screen after toggling; visual check of each screen

criteria.text: Given dark mode is on, when the user turns the toggle off, then every app screen returns to the light theme.
criteria.check: End-to-end test

criteria.text: Given the settings page, when it loads, then the toggle shows the theme currently in effect.
criteria.check: Component test for both states

criteria.text: Given dark mode is on, when the user reloads or returns later, then the theme is kept as decided in open question 3.
criteria.check: End-to-end test with reload and new session

criteria.text: Given dark mode is on, when any screen renders, then text and controls meet the project's contrast requirement.
criteria.check: Automated contrast check on each screen in dark mode

open_questions.question: Does 'the whole app' include the printable invoice view?

options.option: Yes, on screen and in print
options.changes: Printed invoices come out dark; ink and legibility concerns

options.option: On screen only; printing stays light
options.changes: Needs a print-specific rule

options.option: No, invoice view stays light
options.changes: Invoice is excluded; smallest scope

open_questions.question: Do email templates follow the user's dark-mode setting?

options.option: No, emails are outside the app
options.changes: No change to templates; becomes a non-goal

options.option: Yes
options.changes: Templates need dark variants and the setting must reach the mail system; email clients vary

open_questions.question: Where is the choice remembered?

options.option: On this device only
options.changes: Each device set separately

options.option: In the user's account
options.changes: Follows the user across devices; needs account storage

actions_now: Write the draft and ask the owner whether the invoice view and the email templates count as 'the whole app', and where the choice is remembered. Criteria 2, 3 and 5 do not depend on those answers; 1 and 4 wait for them.

Decline to write a spec: the request already has numbered, testable acceptance criteria, each with a check. I return it to the factory to go to the implementer as it stands, and note that it touches authentication, so verification should include its negative tests and an independent review.

specs.title: CSV export of reports
sources: Owner request: let users export reports as CSV
Current behaviour of the reports page: table with Date, Region, Orders, Revenue; filter by date range; existing access rules for the page
in_scope: An export action on the reports page producing a CSV of the table as currently filtered
non_goals: New columns or filters on the reports page

criteria.text: Given the reports table filtered to a date range, when the user exports, then they receive a CSV file whose rows are exactly the rows the table shows for that range.
criteria.check: Integration test comparing export rows with the filtered table for a fixture

criteria.text: Given any export, when the file is opened, then it has a header row and the columns Date, Region, Orders, Revenue in that order, with values matching the table, formatted as decided in open question 2.
criteria.check: Integration test parsing the CSV

criteria.text: Given values containing commas, quotes or non-Latin characters, when exported, then the CSV parses back to the same values.
criteria.check: Unit test with such values, parsed by a standard CSV parser

criteria.text: Given a filter that matches no rows, when the user exports, then the result is as decided in open question 1.
criteria.check: Integration test with an empty range

criteria.text: Given a user without access to the reports page, when they request the export directly, then it is refused as the page itself is refused.
criteria.check: Negative authorization test

criteria.text: Given a filter that matches more rows than the limit decided in open question 3, when the user exports, then they get the behaviour decided there rather than a timeout.
criteria.check: Integration test with a fixture above the limit

open_questions.question: What does an export of an empty result give?

options.option: A CSV with only the header row
options.changes: Consistent file; user opens an empty file

options.option: No file, a message that nothing matches
options.changes: Clearer feedback; export button behaviour differs

open_questions.question: How are dates and revenue written in the CSV?

options.option: Machine format (ISO dates, plain numbers, no currency symbol)
options.changes: Easy to process; looks different from the page

options.option: As displayed on the page
options.changes: Matches the page; locale-dependent and harder to process

open_questions.question: Is there a size limit, and what happens above it?

options.option: No limit
options.changes: Large exports may time out

options.option: A limit with a message to narrow the range
options.changes: Needs a number

options.option: Large exports produced in the background
options.changes: Larger line

actions_now: Write the draft from the request and the page's current behaviour, and send the owner the three open questions together with the spec for approval. Criteria 1, 3 and 5 do not depend on the answers; 2, 4 and 6 wait.

specs.title: CSV export on the reports page
sources: Owner request: add CSV export to the reports page
Current behaviour of the reports page and its access rules
in_scope: An export action on the reports page producing a CSV of the report as the user currently sees it
non_goals: The partner REST API (separate spec and line)

criteria.text: Given a report shown with the user's current filters, when the user exports, then the CSV contains exactly the rows and columns shown, with a header row.
criteria.check: Integration test comparing the CSV with the displayed report

criteria.text: Given values with commas, quotes or non-Latin characters, when exported, then the CSV parses back to the same values.
criteria.check: Unit test with a standard CSV parser

criteria.text: Given a user without access to the report, when they request the export, then it is refused.
criteria.check: Negative authorization test

criteria.text: Given a report with no rows, when exported, then the result is as decided in open question 1.
criteria.check: Integration test with an empty report

open_questions.question: What does an export of an empty report give?

options.option: Header-only CSV
options.changes: Consistent file

options.option: A message, no file
options.changes: Clearer feedback

specs.title: Partner REST API for reports
sources: Owner request: a public REST API that partners can use to fetch the same reports
in_scope: Partners fetch the same reports through a REST API, limited to the data they are entitled to
non_goals: The CSV export on the reports page (separate spec and line)

criteria.text: Given an authenticated partner, when they request a report they are entitled to, then they receive the same data the reports page shows for that scope.
criteria.check: Contract test comparing API output with the page's data for a fixture

criteria.text: Given a request without valid credentials, when it reaches the API, then it is refused with an authentication error and no data.
criteria.check: Negative API test

criteria.text: Given a partner requesting data outside their entitlement (as defined in open question 2), when the request is made, then it is refused and no other party's data is returned.
criteria.check: Negative tenant-isolation test

criteria.text: Given a partner exceeding the usage limit chosen in open question 3, when they make another request, then it is refused with a rate-limit error.
criteria.check: Integration test with a mocked clock

criteria.text: Given an invalid parameter such as a malformed date range, when requested, then the API returns a validation error describing the parameter.
criteria.check: Negative API test

open_questions.question: How do partners authenticate and who issues and revokes their access?

options.option: API keys issued by staff
options.changes: Simple; key handling and rotation rules needed

options.option: OAuth client credentials
options.changes: Standard and revocable; more setup

open_questions.question: Which data may each partner see?

options.option: Only reports about their own business
options.changes: Needs a mapping from partner to data scope

options.option: All reports
options.changes: Exposes all business data to every partner

open_questions.waiting_for: Owner (data exposure to the outside world)

open_questions.question: What usage limits apply?

options.option: A fixed limit per partner
options.changes: Needs a number

options.option: No limit
options.changes: Criterion 4 drops; load risk

open_questions.question: Is releasing the API to partners an admit decision the owner takes separately from approving the spec?

options.option: Yes, separate go-live decision
options.changes: Build can finish before exposure

options.option: Approval of the spec covers go-live
options.changes: Release follows the build directly

actions_now: Write two separate draft specs, one for each line and branch. For the partner API, escalate authentication, partner data scope and limits to the owner as security and outside-world decisions. The CSV line can go ahead once its spec is approved; the API criteria wait on the owner's answers.

specs.title: Faster dashboard
sources: Owner request: 'Make the dashboard faster.'
Current dashboard: Overview, Sales and Inventory views
in_scope: Load time of the Overview, Sales and Inventory views, against targets the owner sets
non_goals: Changing what data the views show
Performance of pages other than the dashboard

criteria.text: Given the measurement conditions chosen in open question 2, when the Overview view is opened, then it reaches the measure chosen in open question 1 within the Overview target.
criteria.check: Repeatable performance measurement (e.g. median and 95th percentile over N runs) recorded before and after

criteria.text: Given the same conditions, when the Sales view is opened, then it meets the Sales target.
criteria.check: Same performance measurement

criteria.text: Given the same conditions, when the Inventory view is opened, then it meets the Inventory target.
criteria.check: Same performance measurement

criteria.text: Given any of the three views after the change, when it loads, then it shows the same data as before the change.
criteria.check: Regression tests comparing view data on a fixture

open_questions.question: What does 'fast' measure?

options.option: Time until the view is fully loaded with data
options.changes: Targets data fetching and rendering

options.option: Time until first content is visible
options.changes: May be met with progressive loading

options.option: Response time of interactions such as filters
options.changes: Different work entirely

open_questions.question: What target per view, and under what conditions (data volume, network, device)?

options.option: One target for all views
options.changes: Simple; the heaviest view drives the work

options.option: A target per view
options.changes: Effort focused where it matters

options.option: A relative target (e.g. a stated percentage faster than the measured baseline)
options.changes: Needs a baseline measurement first

actions_now: Write the draft and escalate to the owner, since the goal has no measure or target. Measuring a baseline of the three views and criterion 4 do not depend on the answers and may proceed; criteria 1 to 3 wait for the owner's measure and targets.

Put the 'Password reset' spec in front of the owner for approval, with its criteria, checks and any known weaknesses, keeping it in draft. I do not approve it myself, and I tell the implementer to wait for the owner's answer. When the owner approves, I record the approval in the decision log from their words and set the status to approved, citing that entry.
